subject: math
title: A-Math quadratics: completing the square, discriminant and inequalities Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: The equation x^2 + 1 = 0 has discriminant D = -4. What are its roots?

choices.text: There are no roots and no solution
Two complex roots, x = i and x = -i
Two real roots, x = 1 and x = -1

questions.misconception: A negative discriminant means the equation has no solution.
questions.feedback: If you said there is no solution, that is the trap: A negative discriminant means the equation has no solution. Reteach point: No real roots is not no solution: the equation still has two complex roots. For x^2 + 1 = 0 the roots are x = +/-i.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain how to complete the square for x^2 + 6x.
questions.answer: Halve the coefficient of x to get 3, then add the missing corner 3^2 = 9, giving x^2 + 6x + 9 = (x+3)^2.
questions.feedback: A strong answer halves 6 to get 3 and adds 3^2 = 9. An answer that adds 36 has squared the whole coefficient instead of half of it.

questions.prompt: A quadratic has D = 0. How many real roots does it have?
questions.feedback: D = 0 means the parabola just touches the x-axis, so there is one repeated real root. D > 0 gives two real roots and D < 0 gives no real roots.

questions.prompt: State the solution of x^2 - 4 > 0 and how you found it.
questions.answer: x < -2 or x > 2, found by taking the roots -2 and 2 and testing each region of the number line.
questions.feedback: The roots -2 and 2 split the line into three regions; testing shows only the two outer regions satisfy x^2 - 4 > 0, so the solution is x < -2 or x > 2.
